title: RICE WAFFLES
ingredients: 1 cup cold boiled rice.  1/2 cup white flour, and same of corn-meal.  2 eggs well whipped, and milk to make soft batter. 1 tablespoonful melted butter.  1/2 teaspoonful soda, dissolved in hot water.   1 &#160; " &#160; of salt.  Beat the mixture smooth before baking.
instructions: 1 quart milk.  1 cup cold boiled rice.  3 cups rice flour, or enough for thin batter. 1 tablespoonful melted butter.  3 eggs.  1 teaspoonful salt.
1 pint milk.  3 eggs, beaten very light.

Be especially careful in greasing your irons for these waffles, as for all which contain rice.

2 quarts flour.  2 tablespoonfuls lard.  3 &#160; " &#160; butter.  2 1/2 cups sour or buttermilk. "Loppered" cream is still better.  2 eggs, well beaten. 1 teaspoonful soda, dissolved in hot water.  1 &#160; " &#160; salt.  Chop up the shortening in the salted flour, as for pastry. Add the eggs and soda to the milk; put all together, handling as little as may be. Roll lightly and quickly into two sheets, the one intended for the upper crust fully half an
inch thick, the lower less than this. Lay the latter smoothly in a well-greased baking-pan, strew it

thickly with rasp berries,  blackberries, or, what is better yet, huckleberries; sprinkle four or five tablespoonfuls of sugar over these, cover with the thicker crust, and bake from twenty to twenty-five minutes, until nicely browned, but not dried. Eat hot for breakfast with butter and powdered sugar.

If sweet milk be used; add two tea-spoonfuls cream-tartar sifted into the dry flour. It should be mixed as soft as can be rolled. This shortcake is very nice made with the common "black-caps" or wild raspberries.

large cup sour cream or very rich "loppered" milk.  1 egg.  1 tablespoonful white sugar.  1 teaspoonful soda, dissolved in hot water.  1 saltspoonful salt.  Proceed, in mixing and baking, as with the huckleberry short-cake, except that, instead of putting the berries between the crust, you lay one sheet of paste smoothly upon the other, and bake until done. While warm--not hot--separate these. They will come apart easily, just where they were joined. Lay upon the lower a thick coating, several deep, of strawberries; sprinkle powdered sugar among and over them; cover with the upper crust. It is best to bake strawberry shortcake in round jelly-cake tins, or round pans a little deeper than these, as they should be sent to table whole, while the hot short-cake is generally cut into square slices, and piled upon a plate.
